identity.name: NGFW Container Egress to Endpoint Process Causality Stitch — Cortex XSIAM (T1071.001)
identity.summary: A container generates outbound network traffic (App-ID, URL, and DGA-style egress) while the Cortex agent records the originating container process. XSIAM stitches the NGFW session and the endpoint container process on the 5-tuple plus container_id within a 10-second window into one cross-plane incident the DC presents as the stitching wedge.
identity.description: This scenario ports the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab ngfw fixture (container-ttp-netgen.sh generate_network_traffic loop + fw-analysis.yaml) into a Cortex XSIAM cross-plane stitching card on the ANALYTICS plane, mirroring SIM-MP-001's F2 causality-graph shape but joining the NETWORK plane (NGFW) to the CDR plane (container endpoint) rather than to a host endpoint. The lab's generate_network_traffic function loops emitting outbound sessions with explicit 5-tuples (src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, protocol) from inside a container so the NGFW raises App-ID, URL-filtering, and DGA-style alerts; CortexSim reproduces that loop with benign destinations and adds a small set of DGA-shaped hostnames to exercise the NGFW's DNS/URL analytics. The headline is the stitch: the same network session the NGFW logs is also recorded by the Cortex agent as a network event whose actor is a specific container process, and XSIAM correlates the two records on the shared 5-tuple AND the container_id within a 10-second window, producing one incident that shows the full causality chain (container process -> outbound session -> NGFW App-ID/URL/DGA verdict). The detection content is two stitchable XQLs — one against panw_ngfw_traffic_raw projecting the NGFW App-ID/URL/DGA signal keyed on the 5-tuple, and one against xdr_data projecting the endpoint container process keyed on the same 5-tuple plus container_id — and a correlation rule CR-MP-0006 that asserts >= 2 distinct planes (CDR + NDR) under one incident_id joined on the 5-tuple within the correlation window. This directly strengthens the ANALYTICS plane's stitching wedge: the architectural reality a POV must simulate is that network and endpoint signals fuse into one causality story, not two disconnected alerts.

actors.name: Opportunistic intruders operating C2 from a compromised container workload

campaigns: Container C2 egress with cross-plane network-to-endpoint correlation

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-006 — NGFW container egress + endpoint process 5-tuple stitch for Cortex XSIAM validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM ingesting both the NGFW traffic logs (panw_ngfw_traffic_raw) and the Cortex agent endpoint telemetry (xdr_data) so the network session and the container process are both present for stitching.

prerequisites.description: ndr + cdr IaC modules applied so the NGFW/collector sees container egress and the EKS cluster runs the egress-generating workload.

payload.code:
# Container egress generator (benign destinations) mirroring the lab's
# generate_network_traffic 5-tuple loop + a few DGA-shaped hostnames to
# exercise NGFW App-ID / URL / DGA analytics. No payloads detonated.
set -euo pipefail
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  SRC_PORT="$((RANDOM % 30000 + 20000))"
  curl -sSL -m 5 --local-port "$SRC_PORT" -A 'CortexSimContainerBeacon/1.0' "http://testmynids.org/uid/index.html?stitch=$i" -o /dev/null || true
  HOST="$(head -c 12 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n').example.net"
  curl -sSL -m 5 "http://${HOST}/" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
  sleep 1
done
echo "[*] Container egress 5-tuple loop + DGA-shaped hostnames generated for NGFW<->endpoint stitch"

input_variables.name: BEACON_DST
input_variables.description: Benign destination host the container beacons to so the NGFW logs an App-ID/URL session.

expected_artifacts.description: Outbound container session the NGFW logs with App-ID/URL classification, keyed on the 5-tuple.
DGA-shaped hostname resolution that exercises NGFW DNS/URL analytics.

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-006 cleanup complete — no persistent artifacts; benign egress only.'

xql_queries.name: MP-006 Container Workload Projection
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| fields actor_container_info as container_info
| filter container_info != null
| alter pod_namespace = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_namespace")
| alter pod_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_name")
| alter image_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_name")
| alter image_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_id")
| alter container_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.id")
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.privileged")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("curl", "wget", "nc")

xql_queries.name: MP-006 NGFW Container Egress App-ID URL and DGA Signal
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| filter app contains "web-browsing" or app contains "ssl" or url_category != null
| alter five_tuple = concat(source_ip, ":", to_string(source_port), "->", dest_ip, ":", to_string(dest_port), "/", protocol)
| comp count() as ngfw_sessions by source_ip, source_port, dest_ip, dest_port, protocol
| filter ngfw_sessions >= 1
| sort desc ngfw_sessions
| fields source_ip, source_port, dest_ip, dest_port, protocol, ngfw_sessions

xql_queries.name: MP-006 Endpoint Container Process Network Causality
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter actor_container_info != null
| alter container_id = json_extract_scalar(actor_container_info, "$.id")
| alter five_tuple = concat(action_local_ip, ":", to_string(action_local_port), "->", action_remote_ip, ":", to_string(action_remote_port), "/", action_network_protocol)
| comp count() as endpoint_sessions by container_id, action_local_ip, action_local_port, action_remote_ip, action_remote_port
| filter endpoint_sessions >= 1
| fields container_id, action_local_ip, action_local_port, action_remote_ip, action_remote_port, endpoint_sessions

correlation_rules.name: NGFW Container Egress to Endpoint Process Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(MP-006 NGFW Container Egress App-ID URL and DGA Signal) AND XQL(MP-006 Endpoint Container Process Network Causality) joined on the shared 5-tuple (source_ip, source_port, dest_ip, dest_port, protocol) plus container_id within a 10-second correlation window — asserts >= 2 distinct planes (CDR endpoint + NDR network) under one incident_id, producing the container-process -> outbound-session -> NGFW App-ID/URL/DGA causality chain.

threat_scenarios.name: NGFW-to-Endpoint Container Causality Stitching
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex XSIAM stitches an NGFW App-ID/URL/DGA session and the endpoint container process that originated it into one cross-plane incident on the shared 5-tuple + container_id, proving network and endpoint signals fuse into one causality story.

threat_steps.objective: The NGFW container egress and the endpoint container process are both captured on the shared 5-tuple.
preconditions: ndr + cdr IaC fixtures applied with the egress-generating workload running.
steps: Run the container egress 5-tuple loop + DGA-shaped hostnames.
Observe both the NGFW signal XQL and the endpoint container-process XQL return rows for the same 5-tuple.
success_criteria: XQL `MP-006 NGFW Container Egress App-ID URL and DGA Signal` returns >= 1 session.
XQL `MP-006 Endpoint Container Process Network Causality` returns >= 1 session for the same 5-tuple.

threat_steps.objective: XSIAM stitches the two planes into one incident within the 10s window.
preconditions: Correlation CR-MP-0006 enabled with a 10-second window.
steps: Observe CR-MP-0006 raise one incident joining the NGFW and endpoint records.
Verify the incident shows >= 2 distinct planes (CDR + NDR).
success_criteria: Correlation CR-MP-0006 raises exactly one incident_id for the shared 5-tuple.
The incident represents >= 2 distinct planes (CDR endpoint + NDR network).

preventive_controls: Apply egress network policy restricting each container to its declared destinations so anomalous outbound sessions are blocked at the mesh.
Enable NGFW App-ID, URL-filtering, and DNS-security (DGA) profiles on all container egress paths.
Forward NGFW traffic logs and the Cortex agent endpoint telemetry to the same XSIAM tenant so cross-plane stitching is possible.
detection_engineering: Project NGFW sessions and endpoint container-process network events onto a common 5-tuple key for stitching.
Correlate the two planes within a tight (10s) window on the 5-tuple plus container_id.
Alert when a container-origin process is the actor behind an NGFW App-ID/URL/DGA verdict.
